speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Well, look at that... {ad}! Nobody's seen your face in town since the bank put a lock on your door.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Didn't have the face to show, Sully.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Nonsense. The drought didn't pick anybody out; half the plains went under that summer.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I'm looking for work. Anything.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: My place could use a hand. The bed creaks some, and I do the cooking. Decide accordingly.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: But before we head out, show your face around town. Plenty of folks asked after you; slip away quiet and the gossip will never end.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Say hello to a few people. I'll be out front of the store.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: When did you last eat?

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Yesterday... I think.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: "I think." Your face already told me.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Here, take this. It's not a loan, not an advance. A hungry hand does no work, that's all.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Buy something that keeps. Beans, hardtack... Don't waste it on sweets.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: No canteen either? Take mine. I'll get another, I lose one every year anyway.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Hah. Now you look a little more human.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Fill it wherever you find water. Nobody buys you a drink in the desert.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Right then. The ranch is out of town. Too far to walk, we'll ride.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: No horse, huh? Take Coal. She's old but she knows the way. Complains less than I do.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Where's your horse? Whistle, it'll come. A good horse doesn't keep its rider waiting.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Follow me. Though you know these trails better than I do; if I get turned around at the fork, you set me straight.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Thirty-one years since I first rode this road.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Martha sat up on the wagon and I walked alongside. We couldn't afford a horse.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: And now?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Now there's a horse.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: ...No Martha.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Anyway. The chickens are waiting on me, and me on them.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Shh. You hear that?

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The wind?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Wind doesn't carry off chickens.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Coyotes. Third night running. To the coop, quick!

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: No gun? Here, my father's pistol. I want it back, mind.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Here we are. A house, a barn, a well, a bunch of chickens and me. We're all a little tired.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Tie up your horse and come in. Sun's about to set.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: That's one! Keep at it!

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Not bad. At your age I hit a chicken every other shot.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: The larder's empty too, I might as well say it. There's game past the hill. Easier to sneak up on at dusk.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: This meat'll last us a week. Take the pelt to the butcher in town, he pays well.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: You're not coming?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: There are folks in town... I can't look in the eye right now. I'll explain later. Go on.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Back already? The butcher didn't swindle you, did he?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Come, sit down. It's a long night.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: There's something I need to tell you. You deserve to hear it.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Last month I was riding to the bank. Had the deed on me; needed to show it for a loan.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Three riders came out on the road. The one in front had a red beard. He was laughing.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: What did they take?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: My wallet. My watch. And the deed.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Whoever holds the deed holds the land, so they say. This house, those chickens, Martha's grave... all of it hangs on a scrap of paper.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Didn't you go to the sheriff?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: I did. "I don't have the men, Sully," he says. Thirty years I paid my taxes, and he doesn't have the men.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Anyway. Get up early tomorrow. The bank wants its interest, and the barn wants a roof.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Morning. No coffee, it's gone. And the roof leaks.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Give me four hours. I'll pay what I can find; little money, but honest.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Good work. That roof'll hold another ten years... or one winter.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Let's ride into town. I'll talk to the sheriff once more; this time I'll have someone with me.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Let me do the talking. The sheriff likes me.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Well... he used to.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Stop by the bank first. Don't carry cash around; pockets around here empty themselves.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Sully. The deed again?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: The deed again. This time I've got a witness.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: What good's a witness? Nobody knows where Jack's camp is. Those who do won't say.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Is there a bounty on him?

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: There is. Check the board. Full reward to whoever brings him in alive... but nobody does.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Twenty-five dollars. So my deed isn't even worth twenty-five dollars.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Let's go to the saloon tonight. What the sheriff doesn't know, the bartender does.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Buy a drink at the bar. Then keep quiet.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Keep quiet?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: People can't stand silence. They'll say anything to fill it.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: {kamp}... I knew it. The old hunters' campsite.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: You don't go at men like that at night. We'll camp halfway and move in at dawn.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Take these. My father's binoculars, my old bedroll and some supper. The bedroll's older than you, treat it kindly.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: At your age I slept on the ground like this too. My back hurt less.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Why are you helping me, Sully? From the very first day.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Couldn't say.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Maybe I'm paying back the help nobody gave me. Maybe I was just looking for someone to talk to.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Eat something, then sleep. I'll keep watch; I can't sleep anyway.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Four of them. One on watch, and he's dozing.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: See the red one? By the fire, standing.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: I want him alive, {ad}. His corpse would give me back the deed, but it can't answer for anything.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: And the others?

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: The others are your call. I'll be with the horses; if I hear shots, I'll come.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Take this lasso too. You know how to tie a man, don't you? If not, you'll learn.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Four men... Jack's by the fire.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Red Jack. And alive! Ten years I've waited at this desk for this.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Tell Sully... Never mind, I'll tell him myself. I owe him that much.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Red Jack... Wish he was still breathing. Still, it's something.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I think you lost this.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: That's mine... Martha's handwriting, right there in the corner.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Thirty-one years... and a scrap of paper.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: Martha would've laughed. "Dunham, don't get so attached to paper," she'd say.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: But you did.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: I did. But not to the paper.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: This ranch's door is always open to you, {ad}. Come whenever you like. I'll even buy coffee this time.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Maybe someday I'll have land of my own again.

speaker: Dunham Sully
text: You will. Just don't go carrying the deed around in your pocket like me.

speaker: Baba / Father
text: I'm asking one last time, {ad}. Back east with our kin, there's work for all of us.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I don't know anywhere but these plains, Pa.

speaker: Baba / Father
text: I know. Neither did I.

speaker: Baba / Father
text: Stop in and see Sully in town. He'll be asking after you.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Four months, Anton. This is your last letter.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: "When you reach Saint Clement, find Greta Halvorsen. She'll help you."

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: You... you're Anton's sibling. Same eyebrows. Same "where on earth have I landed" look.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: {ad}. I'm looking for Anton. No letters for four months.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Nor to me. Nor three weeks of his rent, but never mind that.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Greta Halvorsen. The boarding house is mine; since my husband died, my lodgers have been my family.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Get used to the place first. This city likes strangers, but it wants to see your face first. Greet a few people.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: This was Anton's room. The map he left is still on the wall.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Sleep for a night, then we'll talk. A journey tires you twice: first the body, then the mind.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Good morning. No breakfast; there's coffee, and it's bad.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: When Anton first came here, he didn't have a cent. His first week went by hauling crates at the docks.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I don't have much money either.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Then follow in your brother's footsteps. Go to the dock warehouse and sweat for four hours. Nobody asks you questions; your back does the talking.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Look at your hands. Calluses hurt the first day, then they become pride.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Anton used to come back like this too. A man with an aching back, but smiling.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Take these jars. My canned peaches; I make them every summer, nobody eats them.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Sell them. But careful: every shop pays a different price. The dock merchant pays more for food than the general store.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Sell without asking, and you lose twice.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Good. Now you can sleep anywhere. Anton always said, "The West is wide, the bed is narrow."

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Off to the telegraph office. Letters pass through there; the clerk knows every envelope.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The clerk gave me this. From Anton. It came back.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Open it. My glasses... never mind, you read it.

speaker: Anton
text: "Dear {ad}. I wrote that I'm at the mine in Silver Ridge, that the work is hard but the pay is good. I lied."

speaker: Anton
text: "The company store sells everything on credit. Pickaxe, lantern, bread. Then it takes it out of your wages. It never stops taking."

speaker: Anton
text: "A man named Pike keeps the ledger. Whatever I pay, my debt grows. I couldn't save for your passage, forgive me."

speaker: Anton
text: "Don't come. Or come, but don't tell Pike my name."

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: ...That fool. Why didn't he write to me?

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Pride.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Pride never got anyone out of debt. Silver Ridge is far; you can't walk there. You need a horse.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: You don't have enough, I know. Here, I'll put in this much. Not a loan; if it's a loan, I'm no better than Pike.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Tell the stableman Greta sent you. He won't cheat you... much.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Go to the stable and pick a horse. There are cheap ones and good ones; take the one you trust.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Suits you. Give it a name, though; nobody trusts a nameless horse.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: I'm coming too. Not for Anton's rent... All right, a little for that too.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Silver Ridge is beyond the mountains. On horseback it takes days; the stagecoach is faster, and your horse comes tied behind.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: The fare is on me. If you haggle, you can treat me next time.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Look at that. Dust, rock and a lot of tired faces.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Anton lived here for two years.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Lived? People don't live here, {ad}. They pay off debts.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Ask miners questions and they go quiet. Swing a pickaxe beside them and they talk.

speaker: Madenci / Miner
text: Anton? Tall, mustache, always writing letters? He was one of the names in Pike's ledger.

speaker: Madenci / Miner
text: The ones whose debts grow get sent to the old gallery. You work there, nobody sees, nobody asks.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Where is the old gallery?

speaker: Madenci / Miner
text: Outside town. Don't go in without a lantern, kid. The dark in there swallows people.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: There are letters scratched into the wall... "A." and a date. Below it, a tally: hundreds of marks.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: He was counting days. How many days he worked, how many days he paid.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: The tally ends here. Either he paid off his debt... or Pike took him somewhere else.

speaker: Ambrose Pike
text: Welcome. Pickaxes, lanterns, coffee; all here, all on credit. I just write your name in the ledger.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I'm looking for someone named Anton.

speaker: Ambrose Pike
text: Anton... Ah, yes. A debtor. Debtors work for the company until their contract is done. Legal, perfectly legal.

speaker: Ambrose Pike
text: Come to pay his debt? Forty-two dollars. Fifty with interest. Sixty tomorrow.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Come, {ad}. If I stay here any longer, I'll break this umbrella over him.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: A man who writes debts keeps a ledger. If it's not in the store, it's in his house.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Take this. My husband's lockpick; he was a locksmith, God rest him. I've never used it... hardly.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Go at night, when no one is looking. Breaking into a house is a crime; stealing someone's life is a bigger one.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Here. "Anton: debt 42 dollars. Paid: 57 dollars. Remaining: 38 dollars."

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The more he paid, the more the debt grew. The same trick on every page. Dozens of names.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: This ledger... it's Pike's handwriting. Complaints for years, but never any proof.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Bad news: last night, the claim jumpers Pike hires took someone toward {kamp}. "A debtor who tried to run," they said.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Anton.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: I don't have the men, kid. Not even enough to arrest Pike. But if you go, I'll look the other way.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: At my age, I don't do gunfights. But I can stand at the edge and shout; that's something.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: Here, my husband's revolver. Ammunition too. Better if you don't use it; but if you do, use it well.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: I got this lasso from the stableman. Better than shooting a man; a man who's tied up talks in court.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Anton... by the fire, hands tied. Armed men all around him.

speaker: Anton
text: {ad}? What... what are you doing here? I told you not to come!

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: You also said "or come."

speaker: Anton
text: ...I did, didn't I? Lord. You got Mother's stubbornness.

speaker: Anton
text: The first year was good. I was saving money, I was going to buy your ship ticket.

speaker: Anton
text: Then there was a cave-in. My leg broke; I couldn't work for two months. Pike said, "On credit." Smiling.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: And that smile never ended.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Pike ran. He took the company's payroll chest and holed up in the old gallery; he's waiting for his men.

speaker: Anton
text: He has the notes. Everyone's notes in town. As long as those papers exist, nobody is free.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Then we take the papers.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Ambrose Pike. Alive and in one piece. The court will love this.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Pike... won't make it to court. But his ledger will talk.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: By court order, the company is handing Pike's store to the workers he put in debt. Your brother is first in line.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: The deed is in your name; Anton said, "Let my sibling sign." Go to the store, the papers are on the counter.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: It's your store, Anton.

speaker: Anton
text: Ours. Our store.

speaker: Anton
text: I was going to meet you at the pier when you stepped off the ship. Flowers in my hand, fare money in my pocket. That's how I imagined it.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: And I imagined finding you in front of your own store.

speaker: Anton
text: Well. One of us got it right.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: You two are cut from the same cloth. I'm going back to Saint Clement; a boarding house without lodgers is like a morning without coffee.

speaker: Greta Halvorsen
text: I haven't forgotten your rent, Anton. But take your time. New beginnings aren't cheap.

speaker: Anton
text: Mother always said: wherever you go, you take your roots with you. I think our roots have arrived, {ad}.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Thirty years. Every morning the same fire, the same coffee.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Just once I'd like to wake up somewhere else.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: So you're up. Figured you'd sleep till noon like Vance's boys.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Where's Vance?

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: In town. Smelled a "big job". Every year he smells a big job.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: I've sat by this fire thirty years, {ad}. Only thing I ever smell is my own coffee.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Anyway. There's meat in your satchel and the fire's lit. Eat first; a hungry man shoots at the wrong things.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You should know how many rounds your gun holds in your sleep. The day you have to count, you're already too late.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Go on, see to your horse. Only soul in this world that won't turn its back on you.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Take this brush. A horse won't trust a man who doesn't groom it, and neither will I.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: First time I rode up this ridge I was your age. A borrowed gun in my hand, nothing in my pocket.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Any regrets?

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Regret's a luxury, kid. I'm tired, that's all.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: This is my last winter. Come spring, I'm done. Vance doesn't know, and he'd better not.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: We're out of supplies. Dutch can't hunt and Pete can barely hold a gun. It's on us again.

speaker: Dutch
text: Meat! God bless you, {ad}. We've been eating beans for three days.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Keep the hide, it'll come in handy. There's another job tonight: we're nearly out of cartridges.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Someone has to go into town. My face is on every wall, and Vance says "the boss doesn't go to town".

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: There's twenty dollars on your head. If the sheriff's men look at you for two seconds, they'll know you.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Wear the bandana on the road. But take it off before you walk into a shop: nobody sells to a masked man, they run for the sheriff.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Don't linger near a lawman. Buy, leave, come back. If they know you, don't look back, ride.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: Well, well. The old wolf sent the pup to town, and the pup came back unrecognized.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: Tomorrow morning a mail coach comes through. The mining company's payroll is aboard.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Any guards?

speaker: Silas Vance
text: A driver and a coward. Nobody dies, right, Hollis? He's gone soft with age.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: First turn what's left from the old job into cash. The fence doesn't ask questions. And change your look; your description is on everyone's lips in town.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Don't trust Vance, {ad}. I did, for thirty years.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Nobody dies tomorrow. Promise me.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I promise.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: The ambush is where the road bends. The coach slows down, and we'll be there.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Cover your face. Don't let the driver remember you.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You promised.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: ...Never mind. Ride now. We'll talk later.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Nobody died. First clean job in thirty years.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Now scatter. That driver's running for town.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: I counted it. Twice. Half's mine, half's the gang's.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You are the gang, Silas.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: Exactly, old man. Arithmetic isn't for everyone.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: And I heard something: somebody's quitting come spring. Wonder who that could be?

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: I'm tired, Silas. That's all.

speaker: Silas Vance
text: Tired men talk, Hollis. Men who talk hang.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: The price on your head has grown. Money like that draws hunters; outside town, watch your back.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: I'm going for supplies with Dutch. You scout around.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Hunters... Someone told them where I'd be.

speaker: Dutch
text: {ad}! They're gone. Vance, Pete, all of them.

speaker: Dutch
text: They tied up Hollis. Vance called him a "rat", and he's the one who told the hunters where you were.

speaker: Dutch
text: They rode toward {kamp}. I... I can't come. My leg.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Hollis is by the fire, tied up. Vance's men are around him.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You came. I thought you wouldn't. So did Vance.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: He's the one who sent the hunters. Sell you, shut me up.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: There are two roads, {ad}. Both get you out of this life.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: You take Vance alive to the sheriff; for him, the sheriff forgives you.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Or you leave Vance be; you go to the sheriff and answer for yourself. Clean, but costly.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: If I were you... No. This time the choice is yours.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Silas Vance. Alive. Nobody's going to believe who brought him in.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: I'm striking the bounty on your head, kid. Don't come to this desk from that side again.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Vance... That's one way for it to end. I'm striking your bounty; don't let me see you at this desk again.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: An outlaw walking in on his own two feet... Now I've seen everything.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Your debt is paid. Go, live straight.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: It's over, Hollis.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Over? It's just starting, kid.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Thirty years I sat by a fire waiting for the next job.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Now there's nothing to wait for. Strange. Light.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Where will you go?

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: West. I've never seen the ocean. Maybe I'll catch fish; maybe the fish will catch me.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Find yourself a place, {ad}. A door, a fence, a pot of coffee. The things I never found.

speaker: Hollis Crane
text: Take this revolver. I won't need it again; I hope you won't either.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Up! These rails won't lay themselves!

speaker: Mick
text: Sun's not even up yet, Boone.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Up before the sun, done before it sets. A new hand joins the crew today; set a good example.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: You must be the one. I wrote "calloused hands" in the telegram; look at those hands, just as I wrote.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: {ad}. I'm looking for rail work.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Walt Boone. Foreman of the rail crew. Lots of work, little pay, plenty of dust. Still want it?

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I do.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Good. The camp's by the tracks, outside town. Walk with me; walking's free, horse rent isn't.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Here's home. Three tents, a fire and the endless sound of hammers.

speaker: Mick
text: The new kid? Welcome. Stay away from the coffee, I made it.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Mick, Sven, Tomas. Good men; until payday.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Not bad. You set the tie straight and don't bend the spike. Most can't do either on day one.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Here, stew. Mick didn't make it, don't worry. Eat up.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Get up early tomorrow. Rocks fell on the line ahead; we have to clear them before the train comes.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: The slope slid in the night. The track is buried under rock.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: If the line isn't open before the noon train, the company will throw half the crew out.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: I have a pickaxe.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: That'll do for the small ones. For the big one we need something else.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Dynamite. Listen to me, because I'll say this once.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: You light the fuse, you throw, then you run. The order matters. Most men mix up the second and the third.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Throw it at the rock and get at least ten paces away. The blast doesn't care whether it's the rock or you.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: That's it! The line is clear.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: You're good with dynamite, I'm good with numbers. But these numbers don't add up: last month's pay came short again.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: The company paymaster is Cyrus Hale. You'll take him my letter; by train. Ever been on a train?

speaker: Walt Boone
text: The fare is on me. Give Hale the letter and remember what he says. Written words don't lie; Hale does.

speaker: Cyrus Hale
text: Boone wrote again? The man breathes through letters.

speaker: Cyrus Hale
text: "The pay is short," he says. It isn't short, sir; your workers are wasteful. Whiskey, gambling...

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The crew doesn't even drink whiskey at camp.

speaker: Cyrus Hale
text: Then they must be saving. Tell Boone: the chest comes Friday by train, then by wagon from Fort Redstone to camp. As always.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: ...As always.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Hale says we're wasteful.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Wasteful. Mick has one shirt, and he borrowed it from Sven.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: We're out of ties. Sven and Tomas got two bundles ready at the cutting site, but their backs gave out.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Shoulder them and bring them here. They're heavy; don't run, keep your breath. If you have a horse, load the saddle; it carries both bundles at once.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: You've got a strong back, kid. Tomorrow's payday. Or it's supposed to be.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: The chest came. I counted it. Twice.

speaker: Sven
text: How short is it this time?

speaker: Walt Boone
text: A third. They wrote "losses." Travel costs, damp, rats...

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Rats eat money?

speaker: Walt Boone
text: The company's do. Here, this is your share. Don't keep it at camp; money in a tent is like water in a bag: one morning it's gone.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: The second chest that was due this morning never came. The wagon stopped on the road, and the horse came back to camp alone.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: I know Eli the driver; he doesn't drink, he doesn't get lost. Go look. Take this bandage; you'll need it if he's hurt.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The wagon's overturned. The chest's lock is broken... empty.

speaker: Arabacı / Driver
text: Four riders... Faces covered. One put a gun to my head.

speaker: Arabacı / Driver
text: But one of them had the key to the chest. They didn't even break it, they opened it. Only the company has that key.

speaker: Arabacı / Driver
text: One said, "No rush, the train's Friday." Talked like a city man. Ask in town, at the saloon; that kind drinks there.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Someone who talks like a city man... and the company's key. I have to tell Boone.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: If we tell Hale, he'll want proof. We have no proof, and no supplies either. Let's feed the crew first.

speaker: Tomas
text: Beans! Coffee! God bless you.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Keep the wagon. I'll write "lost" to the company; that's what they always write.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: The company has the key, he talks like a city man... Hale came into Fort Redstone this morning and rented a horse.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: There are fresh hoof prints from the robbery site toward the hills. Follow the trail; don't get caught. Just watch from a distance.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Hale. The company paymaster, at the same fire as the bandits.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Our chest in front of him. He's counting money... and laughing.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: I got word and came. When a man steals the crew's pay, the foreman doesn't stand aside.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Move up behind the rocks. Take cover when you shoot; a man standing in the open doesn't live long.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: I want Hale alive. Let him talk in court, in front of the company.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Take this lasso too. I tie down rail cars with it; it'll tie down a man.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Heavy. Good. It should've been heavy every month.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Take Hale to the Fort Redstone sheriff. I'll carry the chest to camp.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: The company paymaster, caught robbing his own chest. The papers will love this.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Here's your reward. And a telegram came from the company: they're asking about the crew's new foreman.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: Hale... He won't make it to court, but his ledgers will talk. Here's your reward.

speaker: Şerif / Sheriff
text: A telegram came from the company: they're asking about the crew's new foreman.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The company wants a new foreman.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: I know. I put your name down.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Twenty years I laid track. I always wanted to be on a train running over those rails one day; never happened.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: Now I've bought my ticket. My daughter's out west, in a town on the coast. I have a grandchild; I don't even know the name.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: The crew is yours. Pay them in full, don't let Mick make the coffee, and always treat dynamite as the last resort.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The wagon?

speaker: Walt Boone
text: I wrote "lost" to the company. It's yours now; haul your own freight, build your own crew.

speaker: Walt Boone
text: The rails run west, {ad}. One day you'll ride them too. Wave to this camp from the window.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Six weeks now, Pa. The cabin's too quiet without you.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Elias Crowe has come down to town. If anyone can find you, he can.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: I said the bow. A gunshot wakes the whole forest; use your arrow on the next herd.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Abel's kid. I knew you by your walk; he never looks at the ground either.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Any word from my father?

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: None. Six weeks. A trapline is ten days' work; Abel was never late.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Waiting in town won't find him. You'll learn to read the forest. Did your father teach you?

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Some. Not enough.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Not enough. Come on, my camp is outside town.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: This is it. Tent, fire, drying frame. Anything more slows a man down.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Look at the ground there. What do you see?

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Dirt.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Crouch. Bring your eyes down to it. The ground talks, but it whispers.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Three deer. One old doe, limping; two young ones. They passed half an hour ago.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: You read that from the dirt?

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: So did you. You just didn't put a name to it.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: A rifle makes a hunter lazy. A bow asks for patience, and patience is the forest's language.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Keep the wind in your face so your scent stays behind. Crouch, walk slow. Draw the bow full, hold your breath, then let go.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Clean shot. The animal didn't suffer; that's the forest's only rule.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Take the hide to the butcher's shop in Cedar Falls. The butcher buys furs too; your father always sold to him.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: A trader always names a low first price. Let him. Just know what the hide is worth.

speaker: Kürk Tüccarı / Fur Trader
text: You Abel's kid? This hide's skinned as clean as your father's.

speaker: Kürk Tüccarı / Fur Trader
text: Last time he came in he said he was heading north, toward Bear's Den. "The Old King is wrecking my line again," he said.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Who's the Old King?

speaker: Kürk Tüccarı / Fur Trader
text: Not who, what. The oldest grizzly in these woods. Ask Elias; nobody knows him better.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The trader mentioned the Old King.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: ...Did he now.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Twenty years he's been in these woods. Two trappers limp because of him, one's in the ground. Your father always let him be.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: We're heading north. But not in that coat; up there your breath freezes at night.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Frost fell last night. Winter's coming early this year.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Your father is up north, somewhere under the snow. Dead or alive, we'll find him.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Alive.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: ...Alive. Have it your way.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Get on your horse and follow me. There's no road up north; we go through the trees.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: My breath is steam. I can't feel my fingers.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Make camp before the sun goes down. You don't want to learn fire-making in the dark.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Good. Sit close to the fire, but don't burn your boots. Your father burned two pairs one winter.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Eat. A hungry man feels the cold twice.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Your father and I came to these woods the same winter. We were both seventeen, and both fools.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Our first winter a wolf pack surrounded our camp. Abel grabbed a log from the fire and yelled. The wolves ran.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: My father? Yelled?

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Once. Then he didn't raise his voice for twenty years.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: ...Shh. Hear that?

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Wolves! Take this rifle, your father's old rifle. I've been keeping it. Stay in the firelight!

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Wolves! Stay in the firelight; outside it they can see and you can't.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: They're gone. Three wolves, but the pack was five. The rest will wait for morning.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Sleep. I'll keep watch; an old man doesn't sleep anyway, he rests.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: It's dawn. See that peak? The misty one. You can see the whole forest from there.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: We can't comb every inch of the forest; we'd run out of life first. We look from above.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The whole forest at my feet. My map isn't blank anymore.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: There, at the foot of the rocks... a cave mouth. Something's glinting in front of it.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Bear's Den. Your father always carried his lantern; the glass catches the sun.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: The cave's on your map. Let's go.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: It's pitch dark in there. Here, my lantern. Not much oil; don't dawdle.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: It's pitch dark in there. You have a lantern, good. Check the oil.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Bones... not fresh. The bear left this place long ago.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: But a man went in. Look at that footprint: right heel turned in. Abel.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: My father's knife... There's a note tucked into the handle.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: "Whoever finds this: I'm heading back to my cabin. The bear is after me. — A."

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: His cabin is to the northeast. We built it together; the roof still leaks, my fault.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Let's go to the cabin. If you find something, look before you touch; tracks get spoiled.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: The door's open. The hearth is cold. Nobody's been here for days.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Look around. Your father never goes anywhere without leaving a sign.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: The journal, the broken trap, the paw prints. The Old King wrecked the line, and your father set out to stop him.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Twenty years, I told you; that bear hasn't feared anyone in twenty years.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: My father isn't dead, Elias. The tracks go down into the valley, and so am I.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: ...I know. I'm coming too.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: The Old King. Standing up he's two men tall. His left ear is torn, a trapper's keepsake.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: You won't drop him with one shot. Shoot from range, fall back, shoot again. Run and he'll run you down.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: And my father?

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: When a bear guards a place, it's guarding either its food or its enemy. Pray it's the second.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: ...It's over. Twenty years. It's over.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Hear that? Over there... someone's groaning.

speaker: Abel (baba / father)
text: {ad}? ...Is that you? I thought I was dreaming.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: It's me, Dad. I'm here.

speaker: Abel (baba / father)
text: The King threw me off the rocks. My leg... Four days I've been waiting on snowmelt and jerky.

speaker: Abel (baba / father)
text: You took down the bear...? Hah. Your mother would never believe it.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Abel, you old goat. Quit talking, save your blood.

speaker: Abel (baba / father)
text: Ahh... You bandage better than Elias. He once tied me to a tree.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: The bleeding's stopped. Come on, onto the horse.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Ride gently; every jolt hurts his leg. But don't stop either. I'll ride ahead.

speaker: Doktor / Doctor
text: A clean break, and the wound is well dressed. Whoever bandaged it saved his leg.

speaker: Doktor / Doctor
text: He'll be in bed a month. Then he'll walk with a cane. And then, knowing him, he'll run back to the woods.

speaker: Abel (baba / father)
text: Six weeks. Every night I waited, I thought the same thing: "The kid can't read tracks."

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Elias taught me.

speaker: Abel (baba / father)
text: Elias? He hasn't said more than two sentences to me in twenty years.

speaker: Elias Crowe
text: Not to you. To the kid.

speaker: Abel (baba / father)
text: The trapline is yours now, {ad}. I'll sit in the cabin giving you advice; you won't listen, and I'll grumble.

speaker: Oyuncu / Player
text: Deal, Dad.
